rechargeable_batteries.rules_summary: Must go to HHW drop-off events. Do NOT throw in trash or curbside bin. Tape each terminal or bag each battery individually before transport.
not_accepted: Alkaline batteries — regular trash is OK
nuances: Prevents fires — never throw in trash
Tape each terminal before transport

locations.name: MCIA HHW Drop-Off Event
locations.hours: Check mcia.org for upcoming event dates

paint.rules_summary: Bring to HHW events. All items must be labeled. Dried latex paint can go in regular trash. No business-generated material.
nuances: All items must be labeled
Dried latex paint is OK for regular trash

locations.name: MCIA HHW Drop-Off Event
locations.hours: Check mcia.org for upcoming event dates

tires.rules_summary: Maximum 4 tires per household per month. Residents only — no businesses. Must see an attendant before unloading your vehicle. Automobile and light truck tires only.
nuances: 4 tires per household per month maximum
Must see attendant before unloading
Proof of residency may be required

locations.name: MCIA Tire Drop-Off
locations.hours: Check mcia.org for upcoming event dates

medicine.rules_summary: Never flush medications — they contaminate waterways. Use designated drug take-back drop-off locations at pharmacies and police stations across Middlesex County.
not_accepted: Needles and syringes — separate sharps disposal required
nuances: Flushing medications contaminates waterways
Many Middlesex County pharmacies and police stations have drop boxes

locations.name: Middlesex County Drug Take-Back Locations
locations.address: Multiple locations — visit middlesexcountynj.gov for full list

household_hazardous_waste.rules_summary: Bring to HHW events only. Never pour down drain, on ground, or into storm sewers. Put materials in trunk or truck bed and remain in your vehicle at events.
nuances: Remain in your vehicle at events
Asbestos must be pre-registered and double bagged
Alkaline batteries OK for regular trash

locations.name: MCIA HHW Drop-Off Event
locations.hours: Check mcia.org for upcoming event dates

electronics.rules_summary: Recycling of computers, monitors, TVs, printers, and fax machines is required by NJ State Law. Contact your local public works department for your municipality's program.
nuances: Required by NJ State Law
Most municipalities have their own program
Check with your town's public works department

locations.name: Contact Your Local Municipality
locations.address: Visit middlesexcountynj.gov for your town's program

textiles.rules_summary: Every resident and business in Middlesex County is required to recycle textiles. Do NOT put in curbside recycling bin. Use donation boxes or pickup services.
nuances: Required by law for residents AND businesses
Clothing does not need to be in perfect condition
Hundreds of donation boxes across Middlesex County

locations.name: Donation Boxes Across Middlesex County
locations.address: Hundreds of locations — check Planet Aid, Goodwill, and local churches

cooking_oil.rules_summary: Middlesex County residents only — proof of residency required. Liquid vegetable oils only. Must see an attendant before unloading.
nuances: Proof of residency required
No businesses
Must see attendant before unloading

locations.name: MCIA Cooking Oil Drop-Off
locations.hours: Check mcia.org for upcoming event dates

paper_shredding.rules_summary: Residential personal paper only — no business documents. Bring in a box or crate, no plastic bags. Maximum 5 file boxes or 100 lbs per vehicle. Shredding done on-site.
accepted: Paper with paper clips and staples
nuances: Stay in your vehicle during the visit
Containers will be returned to you
Paper clips and staples can stay in

locations.name: MCIA Paper Shredding Event
locations.hours: Check mcia.org for upcoming event dates
